subtopic: Deciding what to do with pocket money
subtype: Approach: waiting a few days before buying [Thinking]
passage: The toy robot in the shop window had a sign: SALE ENDS SUNDAY. Vishal wanted it so badly his palms tingled. "Can we buy it now?" His mother shook her head. "Wait three days. If you still want it, we will go." It was Thursday; Sunday felt far away. On Friday he thought of the robot twice, on Saturday once, mostly while passing the shop. On Sunday morning Amandeep came round with a pack of cricket cards. Vishal ran his eyes over the shiny cards and saw that his pocket money would stretch to four packs. "Not the robot," he told his mother. She smiled.

qa.q: How long did Vishal agree to wait?
qa.a: He agreed to wait three days.

qa.q: What was Vishal feeling when he first saw the robot?
qa.a: Eager and longing, since his palms tingled and he wanted to buy it immediately.

qa.q: What other approach could Vishal use to test whether he really wants something, and why?
qa.a: He could write down what else the money could buy and compare, because seeing the choices shows what matters more.

qa.q: How might Vishal's mother feel about the waiting rule?
qa.a: She is hopeful that waiting will help him think, and she smiles when he chooses for himself.

grounding: A boy agrees to wait three days before buying a toy, and by then he prefers to spend on cricket cards.
